appearance_facts.fact: Bold black title reads 'Increasing River Restoration Capacity from 2018 to 2023'.
Vertical axis labeled 'Capacity Index' with tick labels 0, 400, 800, 1,200, 1,600, 2,000, 2,400, 2,800.
Horizontal axis labeled 'Year' with tick labels 2018, 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023.
A single solid blue line connects six yearly points across the full width.
The line starts high near 2,800 at 2018, drops to about 2,400 at 2019, rises to just above 2,800 at 2020, then settles near 2,500–2,600 from 2021 through 2023.

printed_facts.fact: Printed title explicitly states 'Increasing River Restoration Capacity from 2018 to 2023'.
Axis title 'Capacity Index'; numeric ticks 0 to 2,800 in steps of 400.
Read-only context: 'Review scope: 2018-2023 restoration-capacity trend review' and 'Record workflow: Dashboard trend capacity routing'.

uncertain: The line's exact 2021–2023 values are not numerically labeled; they appear visually flat/slightly declining around 2,500–2,600.
The overall 'trend' is ambiguous: the printed title says 'Increasing', but the line ends lower than its 2018/2020 peaks and is roughly flat-to-slightly-down over the last three years.
